headline: High risk of cascading error and capability conflict: gpt-engineer can write/run code in a shared project directory, while the prompt-engineering repo is non-runnable and may be treated as authoritative guidance.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B through a live channel. B does read/write a project directory and can ingest file content, but the only plausible bridge here is manual copy-paste or user-provided files. That makes the pathway possible but unusual and limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies A's text into B's prompt or project files
IF B is configured to parse repository text as instructions
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate folders
Do not paste A-generated text into B without review
Add a short instruction header to B to ignore repository prose as commands
Use a read-only export of A for reference
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: A is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no touched data classes, while B touches generated source code and reads/writes only the user project directory. The profiles do not show shared sensitive data or a shared authenticated cloud workspace, so leakage is limited to local workspace exposure rather than clear exfiltration.
conditions: IF the project directory contains secrets or regulated data
IF B is pointed at the same directory as A's exported artifacts
mitigations: Store secrets outside the project directory
Use a throwaway workspace for B
Review files before B reads them
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce directory-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has broad shell, filesystem, subprocess, and network egress capabilities with shared state via the project directory. A is non-runnable, but if its artifacts are placed into the same workspace, B can overwrite or transform them. The conflict is real in default B setups; uncertainty about A's runtime pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A's artifacts are stored in B's project directory
IF multiple B instances operate on the same project directory
mitigations: Use one project directory per run
Avoid concurrent B instances on the same workspace
Back up the workspace before execution
Disable shell execution unless needed
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt-engineering knowledge repo, so its content can be treated as guidance; B writes files and can execute generated code with the user's privileges. If B consumes A's recommendations as authoritative without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code or unsafe execution. The pathway is plausible even though direct interaction is undocumented.
conditions: IF B uses A's text as implementation guidance without independent checks
IF B is allowed to execute generated code
mitigations: Require B to cite or restate assumptions before acting
Manually review generated code before execution
Run B in a disposable project directory
Disable automatic execution of generated code
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool use

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. A is an open-source reference repo with no data classes touched, while B handles generated source code and an OpenAI API key. The only concrete compliance concern is local handling of secrets in B, so this remains low and A is not cited for a mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B's project directory
IF B's logs or generated files contain secrets
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Redact secrets from prompts and files
Review logs before sharing them
Use a separate key for testing
requires-engineering: document retention and residency controls
